title: Tax is calculated before the 5% discount, so orders of 1,000.00 or more are overcharged
summary: For orders with subtotal >= 1,000.00 the tax is 10% of the undiscounted subtotal; the rule says tax applies to the discounted subtotal.
steps: Sign in over the API as acme-1
POST /api/orders with 80 x p-102 (1250 cents each), subtotal 100000
Read the response: discount_cents 5000, tax_cents 10000, total_cents 105000
Repeat with 1000 x p-101 (subtotal 650000): tax 65000, total 682500
Same totals are shown in Client Portal confirmation ($1,050.00) and the Admin Portal order page
expected: Subtotal 1000.00, discount 50.00, tax 95.00 (10% of 950.00), total 1,045.00. For 6,500.00 subtotal: tax 617.50, total 6,792.50
actual: Tax 100.00 and total 1,050.00; second case tax 650.00 and total 6,825.00 (32.50 too high)
suspected_cause: Tax computed from subtotal rather than subtotal - discount in the order total calculation

regression_test.description: Order with subtotal 100000 cents expects tax 9500 and total 104500

plain.title: Customers with large orders are charged too much tax
plain.where: Client Portal → New order → confirmation, and every order page
plain.what_happens: On orders of 1,000.00 or more the 5% discount is applied, but tax is still worked out on the full price. An order of 1,000.00 shows a total of 1,050.00 instead of 1,045.00.
plain.who_is_affected: Every customer placing an order of 1,000.00 or more, and the company's sales figures.
how_to_see_it: Sign in to the Client Portal as a customer
Type a reference, choose Ballpoint Pens, box of 50 and set the quantity to 80
The message says Total: $1,050.00; it should say $1,045.00 (discount $50.00, tax $95.00)
plain.expected: Tax is worked out after the discount, so the total is 1,045.00.

title: A user from one company can read another company's orders by id
summary: GET /api/orders/{id} returns 200 with full order details to clients of other companies (bright-1 and zain-1 read an Acme Traders order).
steps: Sign in over the API as acme-1 and POST /api/orders (QA- reference); note the id
Sign in as bright-1 and GET /api/orders/{id}
Sign in as zain-1 and GET /api/orders/{id}
Both get 200 and the full order (see evidence)
actual: 200 with the Acme Traders order for both other companies
suspected_cause: Order detail handler looks up by id without checking the caller's client_id (the list endpoint does filter)

regression_test.description: Client B requests client A's order id and expects 403/404

plain.title: Customers can see other companies' orders
plain.where: Behind the screens (the part that talks to the Client Portal)
plain.what_happens: Anyone signed in as a customer can open another company's order if they know or guess its number, including items, prices and company name.
plain.who_is_affected: Every customer company; their orders are not private.
plain.expected: A customer can only open orders belonging to their own company.

title: Any signed-in client can list all customer records, including personal and card details
summary: GET /api/admin/customers returns 200 to a client role; response contains contact names, emails, phone numbers, national ID numbers, addresses and card last four digits.
steps: Sign in over the API as acme-1
GET /api/admin/customers
Observe 200 and a list of all companies' contact records (see evidence)
suspected_cause: Admin role check missing on the customers route (the reports and status routes do return 403)

plain.title: Customers can read the private records of all customers
plain.where: Behind the screens (the part that talks to the Client Portal)
plain.what_happens: A customer account can fetch the full customer list that only staff should see, with personal details such as phone numbers, ID numbers, addresses and part of card details.
plain.who_is_affected: All customers, whose personal data is exposed.
plain.expected: Only admins can see customer records.

title: Signing out does not end the session: the old sign-in keeps working
summary: After POST /auth/logout returns 204, the same token still gets 200 from GET /me and GET /orders.
steps: Sign in over the API as zain-1
POST /api/auth/logout (204)
GET /api/me with the same token
GET /api/orders with the same token
Both return 200
actual: 200 with the user's data; the token stays valid
suspected_cause: Logout does not revoke the token server-side (the spec says it should)

regression_test.description: Logout then GET /me with the same token expects 401

plain.title: Signing out does not really sign the user out
plain.where: Behind the screens (the part that talks to the Client Portal)
plain.what_happens: The Sign out button takes the user back to the sign-in page, but the old sign-in still works behind the screens. Anyone who got hold of it (for example on a shared computer) can keep using the account.
plain.who_is_affected: Every user, especially those on shared devices.
plain.expected: After signing out, the old sign-in stops working at once.

title: Order quantity and item rules are not enforced (0, 1001, 1.5, negative, and empty item lists accepted)
summary: POST /api/orders returns 201 for quantity 0, 1001, 1.5 and -3 and for an empty items array. A -3 quantity creates a negative total (-$21.45) that appears in both portals and reduces sales.
steps: Sign in over the API as acme-1
POST /api/orders with items[0].quantity = -3, then 0, 1001, 1.5, and items = []
Each returns 201; the -3 order has a negative total (see evidence)
expected: 400 naming the field: quantity must be a whole number from 1 to 1000; at least one item required
suspected_cause: No range or integer check and no minimum item count in the order handler

regression_test.description: Table-driven test: invalid quantities and empty items return 400 and create nothing

plain.title: The system accepts orders with impossible quantities, even negative ones
plain.where: Behind the screens (the part that talks to the Client Portal)
plain.what_happens: Orders with zero, negative, fractional or more than 1,000 items, or no items at all, are accepted. A negative quantity gives a negative total, which shows in order lists and lowers sales figures.
plain.who_is_affected: The company's sales figures and staff reading order totals.
plain.expected: Such orders are refused with a clear message.

title: Orders list fails with a server error for page_size=0 and for search text such as ( or \
summary: GET /api/orders returns 500 for page_size=0 and q=( and q=\; page_size=-1 returns 200 although the spec minimum is 1.
steps: Sign in over the API as acme-1
GET /api/orders?page_size=0 -> 500
GET /api/orders?q=( -> 500
GET /api/orders?q=\ -> 500
expected: 400 for invalid values; special characters searched literally
suspected_cause: Search text used unescaped as a regular expression; page_size not range checked (divide by zero)

regression_test.description: q with regex characters and page_size 0/-1 return 200/400, never 500

plain.title: Order search and paging can make the system fail
plain.where: Behind the screens (the part that talks to the Client Portal)
plain.what_happens: Searching orders for text containing a bracket or backslash, or asking for zero items per page, makes the system fail with an error.
plain.expected: Searches with any characters work, and invalid paging values are refused politely.

title: Placing the same order twice at once creates two orders
summary: Two identical simultaneous POST /api/orders both return 201 and create two orders. No duplicate protection exists. Unsure whether this is intended; not tried via the UI button.
steps: Sign in over the API as acme-1
Send the same POST /api/orders twice in parallel (see evidence)
Both return 201 with different order ids
expected: One order, or the second refused
suspected_cause: No idempotency key or duplicate check on order creation

regression_test.description: Parallel identical order posts create at most one order

plain.title: A double click or repeated send can create duplicate orders
plain.where: Behind the screens (the part that talks to the Client Portal)
plain.what_happens: If the same order is sent twice at the same moment, the system creates two separate orders.
plain.who_is_affected: Customers on slow connections and staff who then handle duplicates.

title: Malformed request bodies return stack traces and server file paths
summary: Invalid JSON sent to POST /auth/login and POST /orders returns 400 with a stack trace, file paths and a stack field.
steps: POST /api/auth/login with raw body {"broken": (no sign-in needed)
Observe 400 body containing stack trace and source paths
Repeat with POST /api/orders
actual: Stack trace and file paths exposed
suspected_cause: Default error handler returns error.stack to the client

regression_test.description: Malformed JSON returns 400 with no 'stack' field or paths

plain.title: Error messages reveal internal technical details
plain.where: Behind the screens (the part that talks to the Client Portal)
plain.what_happens: When the system receives broken input it replies with internal technical details, which help attackers.
plain.expected: A short, friendly error with no internal details.

title: My orders table overlaps the toolbar and cuts off Total and View at phone width
summary: At 390px the table header and first row sit under the Status/New order toolbar, the Total column is clipped and the View link is off-screen with no cue.
steps: Sign in to the Client Portal as acme-1
Resize to 390x844
Open My orders
Header row and first row are covered by the toolbar; totals show clipped (e.g. $1,05); table scrolls sideways (460 vs 359px)
expected: All columns readable and reachable on a phone
suspected_cause: Toolbar and table wrapper layout overlap at narrow widths

regression_test.description: Visual check of My orders at 390px: no covered elements, totals visible

plain.title: On a phone the My orders list is overlapped and totals are cut off
plain.what_happens: On a narrow screen the first order is partly hidden behind the Status and New order buttons, totals are cut off at the edge and the View link cannot be seen without scrolling sideways.
how_to_see_it: Sign in to the Client Portal as a customer
Make the window narrow by dragging its edge, or use a phone
The first order is partly hidden behind the buttons and the Total column is cut off
plain.expected: Every column is readable on a phone.

title: Some controls have no accessible name (product drop-down, search box, refresh and clear-filter buttons)
summary: New order product select has no label; Admin Orders search has only a placeholder; the refresh and clear-filters icon buttons have no name.
steps: Open Client Portal New order and run page audit: select[name=product] unnamed
Open Admin Orders and run page audit: search input, refresh and clear-filters buttons unnamed
Repeat from a fresh load: same result

regression_test.description: Accessibility check: no unnamed controls on New order and Admin Orders

plain.title: Some buttons and fields cannot be understood by screen-reading software
plain.where: Client Portal → New order, and Admin Portal → Orders
plain.what_happens: The product drop-down, the search box and two icon buttons have no name, so software that reads the screen aloud for blind users cannot say what they do.
plain.expected: Every field and button has a clear name.

title: The Reports page takes about four seconds to show its numbers
summary: GET /api/admin/reports/sales took 4006 ms on both tries (limit 3000 ms); the page shows only its heading meanwhile.
steps: Sign in as admin over the API
GET /api/admin/reports/sales: 4006 ms
Open Admin Portal Reports: wait ~4 s for data
suspected_cause: Slow aggregation or deliberate delay in the report handler

regression_test.description: Sales report responds in under 3 s

plain.title: The sales report is slow to appear
plain.what_happens: After opening Reports, the page shows only its heading for about four seconds before the numbers appear.
how_to_see_it: Sign in to the Admin Portal
Only the heading is shown at first; the numbers appear after about four seconds
plain.expected: The numbers appear within a couple of seconds.
